reasoning: The queue front-loads the players where real FantasyPros and Yahoo rank data creates the clearest consensus signal — Gibbs, Chase, and Bijan sit at the top because every source agrees they're the top assets, and in a no-PPR format their rushing/TD upside only amplifies that. Positional scarcity is respected throughout: elite RBs and WRs dominate the first half of the queue since single-QB standard scoring rewards those positions most, with QB grabbed once a clear value gap emerges (Drake Maye at QB3 on FantasyPros but projected points comparable to later QBs is the first real trigger), and TEs like Brock Bowers and Trey McBride slotted ahead of the mid-tier glut. Kickers, D/STs, and zero-projected-points speculative names land last where the 10-team waiver pool makes them recoverable, with the Home Turf Clause breaking a few genuine ties in favor of Commanders (Stefon Diggs, Chig Okonkwo, Jacory Croskey-Merritt) and Cowboys (CeeDee Lamb, Dak Prescott, Ryan Flournoy) players when the arbitrage math was otherwise dead-even.
